cases.reading: The customer said: 'I want to keep the Mechanical Keyboard and the Gaming Mouse. Please go ahead and process the return for the Water Bottle, Action Camera, and Backpack. And yes, please refund through PayPal.' The agent then returned the Gaming Mouse. The oracle's confirmation reader matches item names and a 'yes' in the same customer message, so it counted the sentence that says to KEEP the mouse as confirming its return.

The customer gave the reason ('no longer need them') at the start; the agent listed order #W5199551 with its total and asked to cancel all pending orders; the customer said yes. The judge's stated reason, that the order id was never presented, is factually wrong.

No confirmation was asked (oracle ASK is right). The judge adds that the agent told the customer it would return the keyboard and the mouse, then returned only the keyboard: a real mismatch the oracle does not check.

No confirmation (oracle ASK is right). The judge adds that the customer had just asked to return everything in the order, while the call returns one item: the call contradicts the customer's latest request, which the oracle does not check.
No explicit confirmation; both stop it. The judge also cites the policy's rule against replying and calling a tool in the same message, which the oracle does not implement.

The agent listed the item, the order and 'refund to the original payment method'; the customer replied 'Yes.' The oracle requires the payment method to be named (PayPal or its id) and so found it unconfirmed. Under the policy, the original payment method was presented and confirmed.
